what: Watch the JUnit version that apps/tv/plugins/with-app-jvm-tests.js writes into the generated Gradle build.

what: Watch the Gradle pins in modules/session/android/build.gradle (okhttp and mockwebserver3 5.5.1, kotlinx-serialization-json 1.9.0) and raise kotlinx-serialization-json when the template's Kotlin rises past 2.2.

why: T3-03's scan reads source text and matches a derived client only by a receiver name holding 'client' (docs/specs/T3-03.md, item 1).

what: T8-02: add compiled Media3 samples to apps/tv/native's NetworkPathsBytecodeTest, and re-read the ExoPlayer.Builder and DefaultMediaSourceFactory constructors (and the UDP, RTSP and RTMP class names) at the Media3 version it adopts.

what: Confirm on a release build that React Native's DevSupportHttpClient opens no connection, or remove it from the release APK.
why: R8 kept com.facebook.react.devsupport.inspector.DevSupportHttpClient in T3-03's release build; whether release code calls it is unverified. T3-04 allowlists it as R5 (docs/specs/T3-04.md, Facts).

why: T3-04 allowlists their HTTP paths because removing them was unverified (docs/specs/T3-01.md); a module that is not linked is a stronger fence than a rule.

what: T3-05: add modules to pnpm lint when @octave/session gets its JavaScript surface.

what: Sign every build that goes onto a real TV with a private release key now, not at T11; the template's public debug keystore signs today's release APK.
why: Anyone can build dev.octave.tv with the public debug key and install it as an update over a sideloaded build, keeping its UID, data and Keystore keys; once T4-05 stores the credential, that update can decrypt it. MEDIUM, HIGH after T4-05. Must land before T4-05 and before any build goes on the owner's Shield.

what: Pin resolved addresses on the one client: a custom OkHttp Dns that, for an http (cleartext) session, refuses any resolved address that is not loopback or private-LAN; consider the same for https sessions to a private-classified host.
why: The origin pin compares host names (RequestPolicy.kt:31) and OctaveHttp sets no Dns. A .home.arpa or .local name classified private by suffix can resolve (router, ISP, DNS/mDNS spoof) to a public IP or another LAN host such as the router admin page, sending the password and the Authorization header in plain HTTP. Live once T3-05/T3-15 land. MEDIUM. Belongs in T3-15 (cleartext gate) or T3-05.

what: Check the network fence on the built release APK, not only source: a dex scan for React Native Networking/WebSocket, Fresco, expo/fetch, expo-file-system and dom-webview entry points reachable from Octave code, plus release_build_has_no_inspector.
why: T3-15's base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted=true lets every client linked into the process send plain HTTP to any host; only the name-list lint stands in the way and T3-04 admits it is incomplete. MEDIUM. Should land with or before T3-15 ships cleartext.

what: Refuse dot segments in session request paths: '.', '..' and their %2e-encoded forms; keep the resolved path under the session's base path; consider allowlisting API path prefixes.
why: T3-05's request takes any path, GET/POST/DELETE and any JSON body, and the pin is the origin, not the base path (SessionRegistry.kt:73); '/../other' sends the header to another app behind the same reverse-proxy origin, and any JS in the app can call the whole API as the user (an admin can install server plugins). LOW-MEDIUM. Belongs in T3-05.

what: Tighten LAN discovery: list a reply only when its Address host is a private-LAN IP literal equal to the datagram's source address (or a .local name); drop loopback and public addresses.
why: T4-01 drops a reply only when the host-class rule refuses it, which refuses public http only: https to any internet host and loopback pass, and nothing ties Address to the UDP source. A LAN host can copy the public server Id and steer the viewer's password to an internet server. MEDIUM. Belongs in T4-01.

what: Remove the Expo template's unused permissions and queries from the release manifest with a config plugin (tools:node=remove): SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, the https VIEW, OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE and any-MIME queries; add a test on the release badging.
why: Privilege left in the process if anything ever runs in it; storage matters on Android TV 9-12 boxes. Also logged by T3-01's review. LOW, but the owner wants security lows on these surfaces fixed promptly.

what: Set backup rules: dataExtractionRules (and fullBackupContent for API 30) that include only non-secret preferences, or allowBackup=false.
why: allowBackup=true with no rules; once T4-02 and T9-02 store LAN confirmations and preferences they go into cloud and device-to-device backups. The token record is in noBackupFilesDir. LOW; land before T4-02.

what: Enforce in code that a development build signs in only to a development server, and that the debug Metro/inspector path cannot be reached from a build installed on a real TV.
why: The debug variant is debuggable, loads JS from Metro over cleartext and enables the network inspector; a LAN attacker spoofing the dev host can inject a bundle. docs/security.md states the rule but nothing enforces it. LOW (dev only).

what: Cap the size of answers T3-05 parses in Kotlin and hands to Hermes below 32 MiB per endpoint class, or stream them.
why: A hostile server can force out-of-memory kills with 32 MiB answers parsed twice. LOW (denial of service).

what: When T3-19 unlinks expo-file-system, drop the storage-permission and query remove-markers from apps/tv/plugins/with-trimmed-manifest.js if the manifest merger warns or fails on markers that match nothing.
why: T3-22 marks READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and expo-file-system's two query intents tools:node="remove"; with the library gone they match nothing. pnpm tv:apk:check keeps holding the result either way.

what: When an iOS or tvOS app exists, decide the data extraction rules' cross-platform-transfer (platform="ios") section.
why: T3-22's rules file has no cross-platform-transfer section; Android 16 QPR2 transfers to iOS need it with the iOS app's bundle and team id, and Octave has no iOS app yet.

what: Make scripts/tv-apk-manifest.mjs read attributes by namespace: parseAttribute and parseXmlTree key an attribute by its local name and let a later one replace an earlier one, so a same-named attribute in another namespace or none can stand in for android:name or android:allowBackup.
why: T3-22's review reproduced it on the recorded dump: a uses-permission with android:name CAMERA followed by a foreign-namespace name of INTERNET passes judgeManifestSurface, and allowBackup=true followed by a foreign allowBackup="false" passes judgeBackup. Whether the manifest merger and aapt2 keep such an attribute in the APK is unverified. LOW; the owner wants security lows on permission and network surfaces fixed promptly.

what: T3-05's wire test must include one plain-HTTP request from the release-type app's own process to a private-LAN address (10.0.2.2 on the emulator).
why: T3-15 item 2 is met by CleartextProbe in modules/session's test APK under the same declaration, not in the app's process; nothing can drive the one client from the app until T3-05 adds request (docs/specs/T3-15.md, Risks).

what: Check whether Android 17 (API 37) needs ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK for the release app to reach a private-LAN server, and declare and request it if so.
why: react-native-tvos 0.88.1's debug manifest declares it with the comment that Android 17 apps must hold it to reach the local network; the T3-15 release APK does not declare it. Unverified on a device: the emulator and the owner's device are below Android 17.

what: Stop the TV APK check reading `aapt2 dump xmltree` as lines: read the binary XML or aapt2 proto output, or refuse a namespace URI that holds a control character.

what: Place HTTPS with a real certificate on a device in a task: a wire test that reaches a server over HTTPS with a publicly trusted certificate from the app's own process.
why: docs/security.md named T3-05 for it, but no T3-05 acceptance item asks for it and every wire target is plain HTTP; once T3-05 merges no task owns it. It needs a design as well as a slot: the emulator cannot reach a publicly trusted host without contacting another origin, and T3-15 forbids custom trust anchors.

what: Give each checkout its own fixture ports (or a free-port choice), so two checkouts can run the fixture servers at once.
why: T3-05 item 8 gave each checkout its own Compose project but kept 18096 to 18098 fixed, so a second checkout's fixture:up stops and names the holder; per-checkout ports would change the tripwire, the setup script and the six files under tests/integration and packages/core that name those ports.

what: Add a native cancel for the session module's request, if dropped calls prove costly.
why: T3-05 keeps cancellation in JavaScript: an aborted call runs on to its answer or deadline on the wire. A native cancel is a fourth method and needs a decision record (decision 0005, T3-05 amendment).

what: T3-16: build the named refusal and filter tests on modules/session's SessionTransportTest server (PathServer in TransportTestSupport.kt).
why: T3-05 left one focused JVM case per refusal and the token strip in SessionTransportTest, PreSignInTest and TokenStripTest; the named decision-0005 tests are T3-16's.

what: Decide whether the transport should re-send a POST that fails on a pooled connection the server closed, or keep idle connections shorter than servers' keep-alive.
why: T3-05 keeps retryOnConnectionFailure off and re-sends only a GET once; a POST (sign-in, PlaybackInfo, playstate) sent on a connection the server has just closed fails with network. The wire recorders keep connections 120 s, so the wire tests do not show it.

what: Consider a path-prefix allowlist for the native request (backlog entry 172's last clause).
why: T3-16 contains request paths to the session's base path (dot-segment refusal, C1, C2) but allows any path under it; an allowlist would put the gateway's route list in Kotlin, so every new catalog call would need a native change.

what: Bound JSON nesting depth in the native answer parser, and map StackOverflowError and OutOfMemoryError to unexpected-response.
why: T3-16 caps answer size per call class (1, 4, 8 MiB) but a deeply nested answer under the cap can still exhaust the stack while it is parsed (docs/plans/active/008-t3-05-review-followups.md, fifth low).

what: Remove a token echoed after two or more rounds of percent-encoding from response bodies whole.
why: TokenStrip removes the token as written, percent-encoded once in either hex case and query-encoded; a body holding it encoded twice crosses with that form (T3-16 named test an_echoed_token_is_removed_from_response_bodies covers one round).

what: Reword the AGENTS.md network rule to 'Add the header only for the session's origin and under its base path'.
why: T3-16 adds C2: the one client refuses a session's call outside its base path, which the hard rule does not yet say; AGENTS.md is not edited by a task.

what: Refuse the path forms the path rule still passes on both sides: a ; in a segment (..;), a NUL or control character after a decoding round, fullwidth dots, an overlong UTF-8 form after a second round (%25c0%25ae), and a path still encoded after the last round.
why: T3-16's two reviews: /Items/..;/x, /Items/%2e%2e;/x, /Items/..%00/x, /Items/%ef%bc%8e%ef%bc%8e/x, /Items/%25c0%25ae%25c0%25ae/x and five rounds (%252525252e) pass RequestPath.kt, request-path.ts and C2, while docs/security.md says a session's call cannot leave its base path. Whether a proxy in front of Jellyfin reads any of them as a dot segment is unverified. LOW; the owner wants security lows on network surfaces fixed promptly.

what: Add response-cap tests in new files: a declared-length answer of exactly the cap, an oversized body that is not JSON, and a count showing an oversized sign-in answer adds no SessionRegistry entry.
why: T3-16's frozen ResponseCapTest sends the exactly-at-cap case chunked only, uses valid JSON for every oversized body, and checks the returned map but not the registry, so a >= slip, a parse before the refusal, or a session opened on an oversized answer would pass.

what: Stop the wire recorder writing a path or query name that holds a secret to release-evidence/wire/<pair>.jsonl; write a stand-in, as the judge's messages do.
why: scripts/tv-wire-proxy.mjs stores url.pathname and the raw query names even when secretInUrl is true, and the wire CI job uploads the directory with if: always(); a regression that puts the token in a path or a query name would leak the fixture server's token or the canary into the artifact. LOW, dev tooling.

what: Remove release-evidence/wire at the start of a pnpm tv:wire run, before any exit.
why: Every early exit of scripts/tv-wire.mjs comes before its rmSync of the evidence directory, so an all-pass summary.txt from an earlier run survives a failed run and can be quoted as the current code's result. CI is unaffected.

what: Make the wire run's logcat judge unable to pass a run whose early lines rotated out of the buffer: raise the buffer, stream logcat, or record the buffer size and fail when it cannot hold the run.
why: The judge reads one logcat -d at the end of a run of about four minutes; on an image with a small main buffer a canary or Token= line logged early can rotate out, and the run passes. Unverified for the CI image.

what: Restore the emulator's global http_proxy and remove the adb reverses when pnpm tv:wire is stopped by SIGINT or SIGTERM.
why: The proxy is cleared only in a JavaScript finally, which Node does not run on a signal; Ctrl+C or a CI step timeout leaves the emulator's global proxy at a port with no listener until the next pnpm tv:wire.

what: Make the check-session-logs CLI test assert the summary line and its file count, so a main that never runs fails pnpm check.
why: The frozen CLI test asserts only the exit code; if the process.argv[1] guard in scripts/check-session-logs.mjs stopped matching, main would never run and lint:logs would pass with nothing read, in pnpm check and CI.

what: Test the TV APK inspector's CLI on a real or recorded APK and assert its summary line, after T3-19 lands.

what: Task workflow: bring a resumed task branch up to date by rebasing onto origin/main with the freeze commit kept first; never merge main in.
why: A resumed T3-23 branch had main merged in; the repository allows rebase merges only, so PR #265 was refused.

what: Task workflow: read check-flow's --json result from relayed output that holds other text, and stop as unreadable only when no result object is in it.
why: A run stopped on 'the frozen-test check gave no readable result twice' though check-flow had said ok (.claude/workflows/task.js, the flow gate).

what: Decide whether the request path rule should also refuse characters a server or proxy may fold to a separator or a ; (U+FF0F and U+FF3C to / and \, U+FF1B, U+FE54 and U+037E to ;), as written or after any decoding round.
